question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}\ln{\left(\frac{u}{v} \right)} \\ - v e^{- u + v}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=\ln{\left(\frac{u}{v} \right)}$ and $y=- v e^{- u + v}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

the following derivatives. For the exponential component, the product rule uses $v$ and $e^{- u + v}$ as its factors; the derivative of the linear factor contributes the extra exponential term. The logarithm is differentiated directly by the chain rule, on its positive-argument domain.

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=\frac{1}{u}, & x_v&=- \frac{1}{v}, \\ y_u&=v e^{- u + v}, & y_v&=- \left(v + 1\right) e^{- u + v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{1}{u} & - \frac{1}{v} \\ v e^{- u + v} & - \left(v + 1\right) e^{- u + v}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(\frac{1}{u}\right)\left(- \left(v + 1\right) e^{- u + v}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- \frac{1}{v}\right)\left(v e^{- u + v}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(1,1)&=\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(1\right)\left(-2\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(-1\right)\left(1\right) \\ &=-2-\left(-1\right) \\ &=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- \ln{\left(u v \right)} \\ u e^{- u + v}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- \ln{\left(u v \right)}$ and $y=u e^{- u + v}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

the following derivatives. For the exponential component, the product rule uses $u$ and $e^{- u + v}$ as its factors; the derivative of the linear factor contributes the extra exponential term. The logarithm is differentiated directly by the chain rule, on its positive-argument domain.

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- \frac{1}{u}, & x_v&=- \frac{1}{v}, \\ y_u&=\left(1 - u\right) e^{- u + v}, & y_v&=u e^{- u + v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- \frac{1}{u} & - \frac{1}{v} \\ \left(1 - u\right) e^{- u + v} & u e^{- u + v}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- \frac{1}{u}\right)\left(u e^{- u + v}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- \frac{1}{v}\right)\left(\left(1 - u\right) e^{- u + v}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(2,1)&=\begin{vmatrix}- \frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ - \frac{1}{e} & \frac{2}{e}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{2}{e}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(-1\right)\left(- \frac{1}{e}\right) \\ &=- \frac{1}{e}-\left(e^{-1}\right) \\ &=- \frac{2}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $\mathbf{T}$ defined by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}- \ln{\left(u v \right)} \\ - u e^{u - v}\end{bmatrix},
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the input point

$$
\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the ordered input variables $u,v$ and output variables $x,y$, the Jacobian determinant is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u & x_v \\ y_u & y_v\end{vmatrix}=x_u y_v-x_v y_u.
$$

Here, $x=- \ln{\left(u v \right)}$ and $y=- u e^{u - v}$. Holding the other variable constant, we obtain

the following derivatives. For the exponential component, the product rule uses $u$ and $e^{u - v}$ as its factors; the derivative of the linear factor contributes the extra exponential term. The logarithm is differentiated directly by the chain rule, on its positive-argument domain.

$$
\begin{aligned}x_u&=- \frac{1}{u}, & x_v&=- \frac{1}{v}, \\ y_u&=- \left(u + 1\right) e^{u - v}, & y_v&=u e^{u - v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the determinant in this order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}- \frac{1}{u} & - \frac{1}{v} \\ - \left(u + 1\right) e^{u - v} & u e^{u - v}\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(- \frac{1}{u}\right)\left(u e^{u - v}\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(- \frac{1}{v}\right)\left(- \left(u + 1\right) e^{u - v}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the input point into the derivative entries and subtract the products:

$$
\begin{aligned}J(-3,-3)&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(-3\right) \\ &\quad{}-\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\right) \\ &=-1-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \\ &=- \frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
